Welcome to Robert Clack School
I am proud to welcome you to the Robert Clack School website. As a former pupil and member of staff for the past 20 years, the school and our pupils mean a great deal to me. I believe that Robert Clack is a very special place; we have a strong sense of community and strive for excellence in all that we do.
We are committed to delivering a broad and balanced education, one which appreciates the importance of academic qualifications, but one which also recognises the value of vocational qualifications and the extra-curricular of sport, drama, music, the arts and debate.
Our ethos permeates every aspect of life at Robert Clack School and cultivates the values of mutual respect, compassion, discipline, high expectations and aspirations and hard work. By embracing these values, we believe that our pupils will be able to fulfil their ambitions in life, whatever they may be.
We are proud, but never complacent.
Mr R Taylor – Executive Headteacher

Executive Headteacher’s Welcome
On behalf of all the staff, existing pupils and governors welcome to our primary school.
Starting ‘Big School’ can be daunting for young children and their parents and carers, but we will work with you to ensure that all our children enjoy a happy and successful start at Robert Clack Primary.
As the Executive Headteacher, I am privileged to lead a team of outstanding teaching and support staff who are committed to your child’s wellbeing and academic achievement. We will work hard as a school community to prepare your child for their future, by equipping them with the necessary skills and attributes to ensure that they are successful. We would like all of our children to be empowered, confident, tolerant, compassionate leaders of the future who aspire to Achieve Excellence in all that they do.
It is our fervent hope that your child’s journey will start with us in Reception and will continue to the end of Year 13 in our Sixth Form.

We believe that Collective Worship (Assemblies) plays a very important role in the life of our school. It is an opportunity to celebrate all aspects of school life, to support our curriculum and to provide an opportunity for reflection on what is very often a busy, active day for the children.

Robert Clack is very proud of the extensive extra curricular opportunities that our pupils have access to. They are able to participate in a very wide range of sports all year round in our exemplary facilities.
The Music department offer students access to learn a range of instruments and take part in choir and orchestra too.
They can also attend a range of clubs which are run before school, at lunchtime and after school. Some of these include: School Council, BBC School Report, Dance, Film Club, Food Club, Art Club, Chess Club and many more...
Please use the links to view our sports clubs timetable and non-sports clubs timetable.

Curriculum and Enrichment Offer
You will have access to a broad curriculum of A level and vocational subjects (both Applied General and Tech Level), combined with extensive enrichment and personal development opportunities.
We know that this combination will allow you to achieve your full academic potential and help you to become an independent and accomplished adult.
Your curriculum will be made up of a mixture of qualifications, enrichment and personal development activities:
We offer a wider range of subjects than the vast majority of other sixth forms. So, whilst we adjust our subject offer to reflect demand, you can be sure to find the ideal combination to match your aspirations.
All the qualifications we offer enable students to progress to high level university, apprenticeship and employment destinations. The A Levels we offer are linear and are examined at the end of Year 13. The vocational subjects we offer are high value and are equivalent to A Levels. Please see our subject pages for further information on all the courses we offer.
You can find a list of University destinations for our last cohort of Year 13 students here.

Careers Advisor - Mr J Hamill
Students at Robert Clack School have access to an excellent Careers Programme which supports them to progress to a range of excellent further study and employment destinations at the end of Year 11 and Year 13.
Students receive impartial and personalised information, advice and guidance throughout their time at Robert Clack enabling them to decide on the best pathway to a successful and fulfilling future career.
The school utilises established links with an impressive range of higher education providers, employers' organisations, outside agencies and our alumni to provide students with enriching and inspiring encounters with employers, workplaces and universities.

How does the school measure and assess the impact of its Careers Programme on pupils?
At Robert Clack we are justifiably proud of our Careers programme and the way that we prepare all of our pupils for the world of work. Our programme has been praised by numerous employers and charities such as Business in the Community. We were invited to give evidence to the Education select panel at the Houses of Parliament as an example of best practice in schools.
We use the Gatsby benchmarks when designing and evaluating our careers programme. The full report is available here. This clearly shows that at KS3 all except benchmarks 6 and 8 are met multiple times and in KS4 and KS5 all benchmarks are met. More information about the detail of these can be found by contacting the Careers Advisor.
The eight Gatsby benchmarks of Good Career Guidance are:
1. A stable careers programme
2. Learning from career and labour market information
3. Addressing the needs of each pupil
4. Linking curriculum learning to careers
5. Encounters with employers and employees
6. Experiences of workplaces
7. Encounters with further and higher education
8. Personal guidance
Primarily, the school measures the impact of its Careers Programme through the excellent range of destinations to which students progress at the end of KS4 and KS5. Careers provision is reviewed annually and forms part of the report to the school’s governors each September. Any improvements needed will be made to the programme offered. The next review will take place in September 2022 and the information in this section will be updated.

The Governing Body of Robert Clack School is a diverse group of committed individuals who reflect the school community they serve. They uphold the school’s values of mutual respect, compassion, discipline, high expectations and aspirations, and hard work. The Governors, in partnership with the Headteacher, make a positive contribution by ensuring that the school delivers a broad and balanced curriculum and demonstrates continuous improvement in its performance. They work hard to meet their collective and individual responsibilities through a number of established committees and regular visits to the school.
Governing bodies have three core strategic functions:
All Governors gain great satisfaction from playing a part in helping to improve the education and life opportunities of our young people. They remain committed to helping the school make continued progress for the benefit of its pupils and their families, its staff, and the wider community.
The term of office for all Governors is four years, with the Chair and two Vice-Chairs elected annually. The full Governing Body meets termly. The Curriculum and Finance & Discipline sub-committees meet twice each term.
For more information on the role of Governors in Barking & Dagenham schools, and how you might become a school governor, refer to the School Governors section on the Barking & Dagenham website: www.barking-dagenham.gov.uk
Please note that when the school has a Parent Governor vacancy, parents are notified and given the opportunity to nominate themselves or another parent (with their consent). If more than one nomination is received, a secret ballot is held. Co-opted Governors and Local Authority Governors are elected by the Governing Body. Staff Governors are elected by the staff of Robert Clack School.
Please use this link to find out more about our Governors and this link to find out about their business and pecuniary interests

Carley Monk (Chair of Governors)
Carley attended Robert Clack School as a pupil, and currently has one child at the School. Her experience and knowledge in business administration, customer service and SEND are relevant to her role as Co-opted Governor at the school. Carley strongly believes that all pupils should be supported at school to enable them to reach their full potential, and that their mental health and well-being is of paramount importance alongside this.
Mr Muhammad Al-Mamun
I am a teacher with over ten years of experience across a range of school settings. I have worked with children from diverse backgrounds and supported them academically, socially and emotionally. My work has focused on improving outcomes for young people while helping them build confidence, resilience and strong communication skills. Alongside my teaching experience, I have a background in mental health, clinical psychology and counselling. This has given me a strong understanding of wellbeing in education and the importance of supporting the whole child, not just academic progress. I am also a parent, and my eldest daughter attends Robert Clack. This gives me a direct connection to the school community and a personal commitment to its continued success. I want to help strengthen the partnership between parents, staff and the wider community so that every child has the opportunity to thrive.
Dele has lived in the Borough for the past six years and is the father of four children. He currently works as a Mainline Train Driver on the Elizabeth Line and has previously held roles in compliance and loss prevention. Dele holds a BA (Hons) in Business Management and has a strong interest in governance and community engagement. He is keen to contribute his professional experience and local perspective to the Governing Board.
As a Co-opted Governor, Dele looks forward to supporting the continued success of Robert Clack School and contributing to the work of the Governing Board.
David lived in Barking and Dagenham for over 20 years and worked in the Borough for 16 of those. He has two children, both of which grew up in the borough. David has served for over 20 years on the board of Governors for Robert Clack School, with three of those as Chair. David works as a “Quality Director - Europe & South America” for probably the largest producer of Colour in the world.
Roger lived in Dagenham with his wife for 35 years. Both Roger and his wife worked in Dagenham until 2008 when they moved to Epping. Roger has served on the Governing Body for over 25 years. He has relatives and friends in Dagenham, and visits frequently. Roger’s interests include being Secretary of an angling club. Roger is a retired Quantity Surveyor and does not have any business interests that may conflict with the school.
Isobel has lived in Dagenham all her life and attended Robert Clack School from 2015 to 2022. Having grown up within the local community, she has developed a strong passion for supporting young people and promoting children’s wellbeing. Isobel is committed to ensuring that every child feels seen, heard, and valued, and believes that all young people should have the opportunity to thrive. Having previously worked in the School’s front office, and now as Pastoral Coordinator, she has gained valuable experience and a broad understanding of the day-to-day running of the school. This has provided her with insight into the needs of students, staff, parents, and the wider community, enabling her to make informed and balanced judgements while supporting the School’s ongoing development. As a Staff Governor, she looks forward to supporting the School community both pastorally and strategically, helping to create an inclusive environment where every student can reach their full potential.
Mr Hemaida works for the NHS as a Senior Nurse Manager. He is a qualified quality improvement leader and an expert in healthcare transformation, holding a Master Black Belt Level 6 qualification in Lean Six Sigma. He is currently pursuing a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Healthcare.
Mr Hemaida has been serving as a Parent Governor at Robert Clack School since 2018, demonstrating a strong commitment to promoting continuous improvement in the school’s performance and making a positive contribution to the education of its pupils.
Jade attended Robert Clack School as a pupil and currently has a child who attends the Primary School. Jade is a School Business Manager at another School in the Local Authority and is able to bring experience in financial planning and the day-to-day operational aspects of the school, giving her a solid understanding on how schools function behind the scenes. Jade hopes to share this knowledge in her role as Parent Governor. Jade is passionate about ensuring every child has the opportunity to reach their full potential.
Lisa has 2 children and lived in the Borough for 40 years until recently moving. Lisa has worked at Robert Clack Primary School since it opened in 2021. Achieve Excellence Mentoring
'I think all students should experience a mentoring session' Year 11 Student
'I think I have actually learnt how to revise and my time management has definitely improved. I feel like I can comprehend most things I get taught.'
As part of our work in the Achieve Excellence and understanding the importance of students being supported as early as Year 7 to improve their learning behaviours when falling behind, we have a multi-structured mentoring provision that includes Full Time Mentors from Robert Clack and the National Tutoring Programme as well as using existing teaching staff (Form Tutors and KS5 tutors) to provide one to one support to students that need it.
Through a warm and welcoming learning environment, pupils are supported academically and pastorally so as to become equipped with the necessary interpersonal skills and qualities needed to become commendable citizens with their local communities and beyond so that they can thrive and fulfil their aspirations. Students are actively taught how to:
· develop routines and become organised
· identify their strengths and weaknesses, monitor their progress and set targets
· demonstrate resilience and self-discipline
· develop their study skills inside and outside the classroom
This allows our students to build their confidence and develop the necessary skills to succeed in their studies.
There is at least one full-time mentor based at each site every day. In addition to supporting pupils to excel in every subject, they also help students get organised and complete extra study in school by organising a homework club before and after school, as well as during breaks.

Early Years Foundation Stage
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum sets standards for the learning, development, and care of children from birth to 5-years-old. It's the first stage of a child's education. It ends when a child enters Key Stage One (Year 1).
The EYFS Framework not only sets out expected developmental milestones in the seven Areas of Learning and Development but also supports those working with EYFS age children in providing the correct support, provisions and learning environment to best enable children to thrive and develop as well as be happy and healthy!

Our whole-school curriculum has been designed to reflect our school’s commitment to delivering a holistic education, which ensures that our pupils develop the knowledge, skills and attributes necessary to fulfil their potential and make a valuable contribution to society.
Our curriculum intent is achieved through our broad, balanced and appropriate taught curriculum, our Achieve Excellence Programme, our extensive extra-curricular provision and our core values, which permeate every aspect of life at Robert Clack School.
Our taught curriculum is organised into five distinct phases across the five key stages:
Discovering – at EYFS, students are supported to achieve the early learning goals through play-based learning with a sharp focus on building their literacy and numeracy skills. This allows our children to build strong academic foundations and discover the joy of learning. You can find out more here.
Exploring – at KS1 & 2 students are taught and explore a broad, balanced and aspirational curriculum, which covers all subject areas. This allows them to build a strong foundation of knowledge and skills to support them into KS3 and beyond. You can finc out more here.
Experiencing - at KS3 our students have access to 13 discrete subjects and they follow the full national curriculum. This allows them to experience a wide range of subjects for the three years of KS3.
Specialising - at KS4 our students study English, Maths, Science, Religious Education, and PE. They make three option choices from a selection of over 20 subjects. We enable students to make unique combinations of subjects but also offer more specialised courses to help students to fulfil their potential.
Mastering - at KS5 our students select three subjects and have a very extensive choice of almost 30 courses to choose from. Students can study A-Levels, vocational qualifications or a combination of the two. Students are also able to complete the EPQ qualification in an area of their own interest. You can find out more here.
Please visit our subject pages for more information about the individual subjects at each key stage.

Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND)
If you think your child is experiencing problems learning at school, please speak to your child’s teacher as soon as possible, as many problems can be sorted out as they arise. The class teacher will work with you and decide how best to assist your child, sometimes seeking the support of the SENDco too.
In some cases, interventions may need to be implemented or your child may benefit from working with a specialist member of staff. In a small number of cases we may, with parent permission, refer to an outside agency or a formal assessment may be advised.
However, at all times you will be kept up to date with what is happening concerning your child’s education and you will be advised as to the best course of action.
You can also read the School’s Policy on Special Educational Needs & Disability and the SEN report. The School’s policy on Special Educational Needs & Disability is regularly reviewed by staff and governors. For reference, a full copy is available at the School Office and here.
If you have any questions or queries about SEND then please email sen.primary@robertclack.co.uk to contact Mr Andrew Stansfield - Assistant Headteacher and SENDCO and Miss Sobia Javid - Primary SENDCO.

Robert Clack School recognises that some of its students may require extra support and resources to realise their full academic, personal and social potential and is committed to providing pupils with a continuum of support which will ensure full access and inclusion to the National Curriculum. These aims should be considered as part of a whole school approach to Special Educational Needs. The SEND department works in partnership with the Senior Leadership Team, Heads of Year, Subject Leaders and all staff together with Parents/Carers, pupils and external agencies in responding to pupils’ educational needs.
The school is committed to valuing the individual needs and contributions of every pupil to the school community and has high expectations of all pupils, including those with SEN. As a school we take a holistic approach to students’ learning and development. SEND Students are fully integrated within all curriculum areas, in line with the Code of Practice (2015). Our aim is to support all pupils to become independent learners and develop their skills for life.
Definitions of Special Educational Needs and (SEN)
Under the Code of Practice (2015), the term ‘Special Educational Need’ (SEN) applies to a child or young person who has a learning difficulty or disability which calls for special educational provision to be made for them. A child of compulsory school age or a young person has a learning difficulty or disability if they:
(a) Have a significantly greater difficulty in learning than the majority of others of the same age; or
(b) Have a disability which prevents or hinders them from making use of educational facilities of a kind generally provided for others of the same age in mainstream schools or mainstream post-16 institutions.
Children and young people who have SEN tend to have more significant barriers to their learning. They do not necessarily have a disability and many disabled children and young people do not have special educational needs
The code defines four broad areas of need although, in practice, a child may often have needs in more than one area.
